subject: Tenant segmentation, per-customer policies & next steps (recap)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant segmentation, per-customer policies & next steps (recap)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth from our discovery call. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared
- Need strong isolation between customers in a shared instance (data partitioning + routing controls).
- Desire per-customer rate limits and quota enforcement (different tiers: Free / Standard / Enterprise).
- Want ability to route high-value customers to dedicated pools or priority queues during peak periods.
- Concerned about predictable latency for synchronous API calls (SLO target: p95 < 300ms for standard tier).

Current stack
- Streamline Health runs a mixed on-prem + cloud architecture. Core app in GCP; patient data held behind their VPC.
- Currently proxying LLM requests through an in-house gateway; experimenting with caching but no robust per-tenant quota system today.

Success criteria (what success looks like in 90 days)
1) Policies in place to enforce per-tenant rate limits and monthly token quotas.
2) Ability to pin selected customers to dedicated GPU capacity with minimal config changes.
3) Observable metrics per-tenant (latency, costs, tokens) surfaced in Console + alerts for quota breach.

What Redwood can deliver (summary)
- Per-tenant routing and policy engine (route by tenant id, plan)
- Rate limiting + monthly token quotas with enforcement and notifications
- Dedicated capacity / pinning for priority customers + automated fallback to hosted variants
- Per-tenant dashboards and exportable usage reports for billing reconciliation

Immediate next steps
1) Camila to share tenant_policy_matrix.xlsx with suggested default throttles and quota profiles (attached).
2) Streamline to share a short list of 6 pilot tenants by Tue 2026-04-14 for configuration.
3) Technical deep-dive w/ Ben & Dev to cover routing header patterns, auth, and KMS requirements — propose Thu 2026-04-15 11:00 AM PT (optional).
4) Procurement loop-in: Olivia to introduce contracts@streamlinehealth.com if they want a draft MSA + SOW.

Attachments: tenant_policy_matrix.xlsx (proposed tier defaults), redwood-multi-tenant-ops.pdf (ops notes)

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Olivia / Camila —

Quick technical notes ahead of Thu's deep-dive:
- Header-based routing: yes — supporting X-Tenant-ID and custom priority headers is standard. We'll align on exact header names in the call.
- Concurrency caps: Redwood supports concurrent request limits per-tenant and token/month quotas. Concurrency enforcement is done at the front proxy layer; quotas are evaluated against usage logs and can be set with soft/hard thresholds + webhook notifications.
- Dedicated pinning: Two options — (A) automatic routing to a dedicated pool (preferred for minimal changes), or (B) explicit per-tenant assignment in config (better for tight compliance). We recommend option A for the pilot, then optionally lock specific tenants via config after validation.
- Fallback behavior: If dedicated capacity is exhausted, requests fall back to a compatible quantized model with the same API surface. We can expose this behavior in the Dashboard and via response headers so you can detect degradations.

I've attached a sample tenant_policy_matrix.xlsx with example values and a column that maps each customer to routing preference (shared | dedicated).

See you Thu.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
